title: Freezer signers can only be changed by an Atlas Edit Proposal, while each Relayer Multisig's controller may rotate its own signers at will
content:
Three Modification clauses in the same section set two different standards. For the relayer multisigs, A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.2.1.1.5 and .2.5 let the controlling party — Osero and Soter Labs respectively — "change the signers ... at any time, so long as there are at least two (2) signers and at least a majority of signers are required to execute transactions." For the Freezer, A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.2.1.3.5 states flatly: "Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal."

The asymmetry tracks what each multisig protects. Relayer membership is an operational matter internal to each operator; key rotation must be fast, and forcing a governance vote to replace a departing signer would create pressure to share keys instead. So the Artifact regulates only the invariants — never fewer than two signers, never less than a majority — and leaves the roster alone.

The Freezer is different because it is the check *on* those operators. If Soter Labs or Osero could reshape the Freezer's membership, the party being checked would control the checker, and the cross-party composition at A.6.1.1.7.2.6.1.2.1.2.1.3.3 would be cosmetic.

Note also which governance route is required. Not Osero's Root Edit — an *Atlas* Edit Proposal, i.e. ecosystem-level governance. OSERO token holders cannot vote themselves onto the Freezer, so the constraint binds the Agent's own governance and not merely its operators.
description: Emergency revocation membership is entrenched at ecosystem level; operational keys stay self-managed subject to a floor of two signers and a majority threshold.
